dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
Subject to the provisions of section 58, a promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable to bearer is negotiable by delivery thereof.
Exception.-- A promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque delivered on condition that it is not to take effect except in a certain event is not negotiable (except in the hands of a holder for value without notice of the condition) unless such event happens.
Illustrations
(a) A, the holder of a negotiable instrument payable to bearer, delivers it to B's agent to keep for B. The instrument has been negotiated.
(b) A, the holder of a negotiable instrument payable to bearer, which is in the hands of A's banker, who is at the time the banker of B, directs the banker to transfer the instrument to B's credit in the banker's account with B. (e) any particulars to any officer appointed for the purpose of audit of tax receipts or refunds of the tax imposed by this Act; or

Summary of The Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Act, 1985
Purpose & Commencement
•	Purpose: To efficiently and equitably handle claims from the 1984 Bhopal gas leak disaster.
•	Commencement: Deemed effective from February 20, 1985.
Key Provisions
1.	Definitions & Scope
•	Disaster & Claim: Refers to the 1984 Union Carbide gas leak, including claims for life loss, injury, property damage, and related expenses.
•	Claimant: Entitled individuals or their representatives.
2.	Central Government's Role
•	Exclusive Representation: Represents all claimants domestically and internationally.
•	Civil Court Powers: For specified claim-related matters under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
3.	Claimant Rights & Procedural Aspects
•	Personal Legal Representation: At claimant's expense, alongside Government representation.
•	Limitations & Overriding Effect: Specific exclusions from the Limitation Act, 1963, and precedence over other enactments.
4.	Administrative & Financial Provisions
•	Commissioner Appointment: For victim welfare, with duties as per the framed Scheme.
•	Scheme for Claims: Includes registration, processing, record-keeping, fund creation, and disbursement procedures.

Summary of The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine  Act, 2020
Overview
*Enactment: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020, aims to regulate and promote the Indian System of Medicine (ISM), ensuring quality education and healthcare. *Objective: Establish a robust framework for ISM, focusing on accessible, quality education, and ethical medical practices.
Key Components
1.	National Commission for Indian System of Medicine
•	Composition: Chairperson, 15 ex officio Members, and 23 part-time Members.
•	Head Office: New Delhi.
•	Powers: Acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract.
2.	Autonomous Boards
•	Constituted by: Central Government under the Commission's supervision.
•	Boards:
1.	Board of Ayurveda
2.	Board of Unani, Siddha, and Sowa-Rigpa
3.	Medical Assessment and Rating Board for ISM
4.	Board of Ethics and Registration for ISM
•	Composition & Tenure:
•	Presidents and Members with postgraduate degrees, 15+ years of experience, and 7+ years as leaders in their fields.
•	Term: Up to 4 years, not eligible for extension or re-appointment after 70 years.
3.	Operational & Regulatory Aspects
•	National Register: Maintained by the Board of Ethics and Registration.
•	Staffing: Experts, professionals, and employees provided to Autonomous Boards as specified.
•	Meetings & Decisions: Autonomous Boards meet at least monthly, with decisions made by consensus (where specified).
4.	Appointment & Service Conditions
•	Search Committee: Appoints President and Members based on recommendations.
•	Terms & Conditions: Salary, allowances, and service conditions as prescribed.

•	Based on partial context, omitting full functional details, regulatory powers, offences, and transitory provisions.
